risks.risk_name: Stockholders may not vote on initial business combination or may be outvoted by founder shares
risks.description: Public stockholders may lack meaningful voting power on the initial business combination because founder shares are voted by initial stockholders regardless of public shareholder sentiment.
risks.why: Initial stockholders and management have agreed to vote in favor of the business combination regardless of how public stockholders vote, and public stockholders may not even be afforded a vote.

risks.risk_name: Redemption rights may deter or complicate business combination targets
risks.description: The ability of public stockholders to redeem shares for cash may make the company financially unattractive to potential targets or hinder optimal capital structure.
risks.why: Redemption rights could reduce available cash for the combination, limit deal flexibility, or make the company less appealing to targets due to uncertain capitalization.

risks.risk_name: Deadline to complete business combination may force rushed or unfavorable deals
risks.description: The December 22, 2023 deadline may give targets negotiation leverage and reduce time for due diligence, risking suboptimal deals or failure to complete.
risks.why: The requirement to complete the combination by December 22, 2023 may pressure the company to accept less favorable terms or fail to conduct adequate due diligence as the deadline approaches.

risks.risk_name: COVID-19 and market conditions may impair search for a business combination
risks.description: The coronavirus outbreak and unstable debt/equity markets may materially harm the company's ability to find or complete a business combination.
risks.why: The passage explicitly states that the COVID-19 outbreak and market status may materially adversely affect the search for and completion of a business combination.

risks.risk_name: Failure to complete business combination by deadline results in liquidation
risks.description: If the initial business combination is not completed by December 22, 2023, the company will cease operations, redeem public shares, and liquidate.
risks.why: The text states that failure to complete the combination by December 22, 2023 triggers cessation of operations, redemption of public shares, and liquidation.

risks.risk_name: Sponsor and affiliates may buy public shares to influence votes or reduce public float
risks.description: Sponsor and affiliates may purchase public shares or warrants to sway shareholder votes or reduce the public float, potentially altering deal outcomes.
risks.why: The Sponsor, initial stockholders, and affiliates may elect to purchase public shares or warrants, which could influence voting and reduce the public ownership stake.

risks.risk_name: Failure to comply with redemption procedures may prevent share redemption
risks.description: Public stockholders who miss notice or fail to follow redemption procedures may lose the right to redeem their shares for cash.
risks.why: Shares may not be redeemed if stockholders fail to receive notice or do not comply with required procedures for submitting or tendering shares.

risks.risk_name: No access to trust account funds except under limited circumstances
risks.description: Investors have no rights to trust account funds except upon redemption, forcing them to sell shares or warrants on the open market to liquidate.
risks.why: Investors have no rights or interests in trust account funds except under limited circumstances, so liquidation requires selling shares or warrants, potentially at a loss.

risks.risk_name: Limited resources and competition may prevent completion of a business combination
risks.description: Due to limited resources and high competition for deals, the company may fail to complete a business combination, leading to liquidation.
risks.why: Limited resources and significant competition for business combination opportunities may make it more difficult to complete a deal, resulting in liquidation and worthless warrants.

risks.risk_name: Insufficient non-trust funds may limit operations and deal execution
risks.description: If net proceeds outside the trust account are insufficient to operate until December 22, 2023, the company may lack funds to search for or complete a business combination.
risks.why: Non-trust proceeds may be insufficient to fund operations until the deadline, forcing reliance on loans from the Sponsor or management to continue the search and complete a deal.

risks.risk_name: Material weakness in internal control over financial reporting may lead to misstatements
risks.description: A material weakness in internal controls as of December 31, 2022 may cause failure to meet reporting obligations or result in material financial misstatements.
risks.why: The company identified a material weakness in internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2022, and may identify more, risking inaccurate financial statements or reporting failures.

risks.risk_name: Stockholders may not vote on initial business combination
risks.description: Public stockholders may not be afforded a vote on the initial business combination, and even if a vote is held, founder shares can override public shareholder opposition.
risks.why: The company may choose not to hold a vote if not required by law, and founder shares (78.5% of outstanding shares) are contractually committed to vote in favor, meaning approval can occur even if a majority of public stockholders oppose it.

risks.risk_name: Public stockholders cannot evaluate merits of business combination before investment
risks.description: Investors cannot evaluate the specific merits or risks of the initial business combination at the time of investment, as approval may occur without a shareholder vote.
risks.why: The board may complete a business combination without seeking stockholder approval, leaving public stockholders with only the option to redeem shares, not to vote on the deal.

risks.risk_name: Management litigation may harm reputation and business combination prospects
risks.description: Litigation involving management members unrelated to the company may damage its reputation and hinder identification or completion of a business combination.
risks.why: CEO and other management figures are involved in active litigation with dMY Technology and GTY over claims of misappropriation, breach of fiduciary duty, and fraudulent misrepresentation, which could negatively affect perceptions of the company.

risks.risk_name: Redemption rights may deplete cash needed for business combination
risks.description: Excessive redemption requests by public stockholders may prevent meeting minimum cash requirements to close a business combination.
risks.why: If too many public shares are redeemed, the company may fail to satisfy closing conditions (e.g., minimum cash for purchase price or working capital), and cannot redeem shares if net tangible assets would fall below $5,000,001.

risks.risk_name: Redemption volume may force suboptimal capital structure or financing
risks.description: Higher-than-expected redemptions may force restructuring of the deal or costly third-party financing, diluting equity or increasing debt.
risks.why: If more shares are redeemed than expected, the company must reserve more cash or seek third-party financing, which may involve dilutive equity issuances or high-cost debt, exacerbated by Class B conversion anti-dilution provisions.

risks.risk_name: Failed business combination delays redemption and risks share value loss
risks.description: If the business combination fails, redemption of shares is delayed until liquidation, and shares may trade below redemption value in the interim.
risks.why: If the deal fails due to redemptions exceeding cash availability, shareholders only receive trust funds upon liquidation, and shares may trade at a discount before then, causing potential material losses.

risks.risk_name: December 22, 2023 deadline gives targets negotiation leverage
risks.description: The mandatory completion deadline of December 22, 2023 allows target businesses to extract unfavorable terms, knowing the company has limited time to find alternatives.
risks.why: Targets know that if a deal with them fails, the company may not find another target before the deadline, increasing their leverage in negotiations and reducing time for due diligence.

risks.risk_name: COVID-19 and market conditions may adversely affect business combination search
risks.description: The COVID-19 pandemic and unstable debt/equity markets may materially hinder the search for or completion of a business combination.
risks.why: The passage explicitly states that the coronavirus outbreak and the status of debt and equity markets may materially adversely affect the company’s ability to find or complete a business combination.

risks.risk_name: COVID-19 pandemic disrupting business combination efforts
risks.description: The COVID-19 pandemic may materially and adversely affect the business of a potential target company and hinder the ability to complete a business combination.
risks.why: Travel restrictions, unavailability of personnel and service providers, and inability to conduct meetings may prevent timely negotiation and completion of a transaction, as stated in the passage.

risks.risk_name: Inability to raise equity or debt financing due to market conditions
risks.description: Market volatility and reduced liquidity from COVID-19 may make it impossible to secure necessary equity or debt financing for a business combination.
risks.why: The passage explicitly states that financing may be unavailable on acceptable terms or at all due to increased volatility and decreased liquidity caused by COVID-19.

risks.risk_name: Failure to complete initial business combination by December 22, 2023
risks.description: If the company fails to complete an initial business combination by December 22, 2023, it must cease operations, redeem public shares, and liquidate.
risks.why: The passage states that failure to complete a business combination by this date triggers mandatory redemption of public shares and dissolution under Delaware law.

risks.risk_name: Sponsor and affiliates purchasing shares to influence vote or meet closing conditions
risks.description: Sponsor and affiliates may purchase public shares or warrants to increase likelihood of stockholder approval or meet closing conditions, reducing public float.
risks.why: Such purchases may be made to vote shares in favor of the combination or satisfy minimum net worth/cash requirements, and may reduce the public float, making trading difficult.

risks.risk_name: Loss of redemption rights due to non-compliance with procedural requirements
risks.description: Stockholders who fail to follow redemption procedures may lose the right to redeem their shares even if they intended to do so.
risks.why: Failure to deliver stock certificates or submit written requests by specified deadlines, or not complying with electronic delivery rules, will result in shares not being redeemed.

risks.risk_name: Limited access to trust account funds except under specific conditions
risks.description: Public stockholders have no rights to trust account funds except upon completion of a business combination, amendment, or failure to complete by deadline.
risks.why: Funds are only accessible upon three specific events: business combination, amendment approval, or failure to complete by Dec 22, 2023 — no other circumstances allow access.

risks.risk_name: Delayed distribution of trust funds due to Delaware law requirements
risks.description: If redemption cannot proceed as planned, Delaware law may require stockholder approval of a dissolution plan, delaying fund distribution beyond 36 months.
risks.why: If the planned redemption upon failure to complete a business combination is blocked, Delaware law may require submitting a dissolution plan for approval, delaying distribution.

risks.risk_name: Excess shares beyond 20% cannot be redeemed if tender offer rules are not used
risks.description: Stockholders holding more than 20% of Class A common stock lose redemption rights on shares exceeding that threshold if tender offer rules are not followed.
risks.why: The amended certificate of incorporation restricts redemption rights to 20% of public shares unless prior consent is obtained, and Excess Shares cannot be redeemed upon completion.

risks.risk_name: Loss of SEC investor protections due to exemption from Rule 419
risks.description: The company is exempt from SEC Rule 419 protections for blank check companies, leaving investors without certain safeguards.
risks.why: Because the company has net tangible assets over $5M and filed Form 8-K, it is exempt from Rule 419, meaning investors lose protections like restricted trading and fund hold periods.

risks.risk_name: Inability to complete initial business combination
risks.description: Limited resources and intense competition may prevent completion of an initial business combination.
risks.why: The company has limited financial resources compared to competitors, must offer public shareholders redemption rights, and only $750,000 is available outside the trust account to fund operations until December 22, 2023.

risks.risk_name: Public stockholders may receive less than $10.00 per share upon redemption
risks.description: Redemption proceeds may be reduced below $10.00 per share due to claims against the trust account or insufficient funds.
risks.why: Third-party claims (e.g., vendors, target businesses) may reduce trust account funds, and the Sponsor’s indemnity may not be enforceable or funded, with only $300 in cash as of Dec 31, 2022.

risks.risk_name: Warrants will expire worthless if no business combination is completed
risks.description: If the company fails to complete an initial business combination, all warrants will become valueless.
risks.why: The passage explicitly states that warrants will expire worthless if the initial business combination is not completed by December 22, 2023, leading to mandatory liquidation.

risks.risk_name: Trust account funds may be subject to third-party claims
risks.description: Funds in the trust account may be claimed by third parties despite waiver agreements.
risks.why: Vendors and service providers may not execute waivers, and even signed waivers may be challenged in court for fraudulent inducement or breach of fiduciary duty, risking trust account depletion.

risks.risk_name: Sponsor indemnity may be unenforceable or unfunded
risks.description: The Sponsor’s obligation to cover trust account shortfalls may not be satisfied due to lack of assets or enforcement.
risks.why: The Sponsor’s only assets are securities of the company, no reserve has been made for indemnification, and independent directors may choose not to enforce the obligation.

risks.risk_name: Independent directors may not enforce Sponsor indemnification
risks.description: Independent directors may decline to pursue legal action against the Sponsor to enforce indemnification obligations.
risks.why: Directors may exercise business judgment and fiduciary duties to avoid litigation, potentially leaving public shareholders with less than $10.00 per share due to uncollected indemnity.

risks.risk_name: Post-combination write-downs or impairments may reduce shareholder value
risks.description: Post-business combination accounting charges may significantly harm financial condition and security prices.
risks.why: Due diligence may not uncover all material issues, and unforeseen risks may arise, forcing write-downs, restructurings, or impairments that could violate debt covenants and reduce investor value.

risks.risk_name: Insufficient funds to operate until December 22, 2023
risks.description: Working capital may be insufficient to sustain operations until the deadline for completing a business combination.
risks.why: Only $750,000 is available outside the trust account, and the company cannot assure this is enough to fund operations until December 22, 2023, risking forced liquidation.

risks.risk_name: Loss of funds paid for exclusivity in business combination negotiations
risks.description: Funds paid for 'no-shop' provisions may be forfeited, leaving insufficient capital to continue searching for targets.
risks.why: The company may pay for exclusivity rights and later forfeit those funds due to breach or failure to close, with only $750,000 available for all operating expenses.

risks.risk_name: Bankruptcy proceedings may recover redemption distributions
risks.description: If the company files for bankruptcy after distributing trust funds, courts may reclaim those distributions.
risks.why: If a bankruptcy petition is filed after distributing trust proceeds, a court may view board members as having breached fiduciary duties to creditors and seek recovery of distributed funds.

risks.risk_name: Indemnification of officers and directors may discourage shareholder litigation
risks.description: Indemnification provisions may deter shareholders from suing officers or directors for fiduciary breaches.
risks.why: The company agrees to indemnify officers and directors to the fullest extent permitted by law, which may reduce the likelihood of derivative lawsuits even if beneficial to shareholders.

risks.risk_name: Going concern uncertainty due to mandatory liquidation deadline
risks.description: Failure to complete a business combination by December 22, 2023, raises substantial doubt about the company’s ability to continue as a going concern.
risks.why: Management acknowledges that if no business combination occurs by the deadline, mandatory liquidation and dissolution will follow, with no adjustments made to financial statements for this risk.

risks.risk_name: Distributions to stockholders may be recovered as preferential transfers or fraudulent conveyances
risks.description: If the company files for bankruptcy after distributing trust account proceeds to stockholders, those distributions may be clawed back under bankruptcy laws.
risks.why: Under debtor/creditor and bankruptcy laws, payments made to stockholders before bankruptcy could be deemed preferential transfers or fraudulent conveyances, allowing a court to recover those amounts.

risks.risk_name: Board may be liable for breach of fiduciary duty by paying stockholders before creditors
risks.description: Paying public stockholders from the trust account before addressing creditor claims may expose the board to claims of breach of fiduciary duty and bad faith.
risks.why: The board could be viewed as prioritizing stockholders over creditors, potentially leading to claims of punitive damages for breaching fiduciary duties under bankruptcy laws.

risks.risk_name: Bankruptcy could reduce per-share liquidation proceeds to stockholders
risks.description: If bankruptcy occurs before distributing trust account proceeds, creditor claims may take priority, reducing the amount stockholders receive.
risks.why: Trust account funds may become part of the bankruptcy estate and subject to claims by creditors with priority over stockholders, thereby reducing the per-share distribution.

risks.risk_name: Excise Tax on stock repurchases may reduce cash available for business combination or redemptions
risks.description: A 1% federal excise tax on stock repurchases may reduce cash available to complete a business combination or pay redemption amounts.
risks.why: The company, as a covered corporation, must pay the 1% Excise Tax on repurchases, which reduces cash on hand and may hinder completing a business combination or liquidating the trust account.

risks.risk_name: Stockholders may be liable for unlawful distributions under Delaware law
risks.description: Stockholders may be held liable for distributions received if the redemption is deemed an unlawful payment under Delaware law.
risks.why: If the redemption is not treated as a liquidating distribution under DGCL Section 174, creditors may have up to six years to pursue claims against stockholders for the distributed amounts.

risks.risk_name: Failure to comply with DGCL Section 280 may extend stockholder liability beyond three years
risks.description: Not following DGCL Section 280 procedures may subject stockholders to liability for claims beyond the typical three-year limit.
risks.why: By not providing the 60-day notice, 90-day claim rejection, and 150-day waiting period, stockholder liability may extend beyond three years and potentially up to ten years under Section 281(b).

risks.risk_name: Failure to hold annual meeting may violate DGCL Section 211(b)
risks.description: Not holding an annual meeting to elect directors before completing a business combination may violate Delaware law.
risks.why: DGCL Section 211(b) requires annual meetings for director elections unless done by written consent; failure to comply may require court intervention under Section 211(c).

risks.risk_name: Management may inadequately assess risks of target businesses outside their expertise
risks.description: Pursuing a target business outside management’s expertise may lead to poor evaluation of risks and reduced shareholder value.
risks.why: Management’s expertise may not apply to the target’s operations, preventing adequate assessment of risk factors, with no legal remedy for shareholders if value declines.

risks.risk_name: Target may not meet internal criteria, increasing redemption risk and deal failure
risks.description: Acquiring a target that fails to meet internal criteria may trigger higher redemptions and jeopardize deal completion.
risks.why: If the target doesn’t meet general criteria, more stockholders may redeem shares, potentially causing failure to meet cash or net worth closing conditions.

risks.risk_name: Lack of independent valuation opinion may leave stockholders without assurance of fair price
risks.description: Without an independent opinion, stockholders have no assurance the purchase price for a target is fair.
risks.why: The company is not required to obtain an independent valuation, so stockholders must rely solely on the board’s judgment without external validation of fairness.

risks.risk_name: GAAP/IFRS and PCAOB audit requirements may limit target pool and delay completion
risks.description: Financial statement requirements may disqualify potential targets or delay the business combination beyond the deadline.
risks.why: Targets unable to provide GAAP/IFRS-compliant, PCAOB-audited financial statements in time may be excluded, limiting options and risking failure to complete within the required timeframe.

risks.risk_name: Sarbanes-Oxley compliance may increase cost, time, and resource burden to complete a business combination
risks.description: Complying with Sarbanes-Oxley Act obligations may increase costs, delay the business combination, and strain management resources.
risks.why: The Act imposes significant financial, operational, and reporting requirements that increase time, cost, and resource demands during the business combination process.

risks.risk_name: Failure to comply with Sarbanes-Oxley internal control requirements due to target business non-compliance
risks.description: Target businesses may lack adequate internal controls, increasing time and cost to achieve Sarbanes-Oxley compliance before completing a business combination.
risks.why: A target business with which we seek to complete our initial business combination may not be in compliance with Sarbanes-Oxley Act provisions regarding internal controls, and developing such controls may increase time and costs.

risks.risk_name: No specified maximum redemption threshold may allow completion of business combination against majority stockholder wishes
risks.description: Absence of a redemption threshold may permit completion of a business combination even if a substantial majority of stockholders disagree and redeem their shares.
risks.why: We do not have a specified maximum redemption threshold, and we may complete the business combination even if a substantial majority of public stockholders redeem their shares or sell them privately to affiliates.

risks.risk_name: Amendments to charter or warrant agreements may facilitate business combinations stockholders oppose
risks.description: We may amend charter or warrant terms to make completing a business combination easier, even if stockholders do not support it.
risks.why: Special purpose acquisition companies have amended charters and warrant agreements to extend timelines, increase redemption thresholds, or change warrant terms, and we may do the same to facilitate a deal.

risks.risk_name: Lower amendment threshold for pre-business combination provisions enables easier changes against stockholder interests
risks.description: Provisions governing pre-business combination activity can be amended with only 65% stockholder approval, making changes easier than for other SPACs.
risks.why: Amendments to pre-business combination provisions require approval of only 65% of outstanding common stock, a lower threshold than some other SPACs, increasing likelihood of changes stockholders oppose.

risks.risk_name: Initial stockholders' control may lead to decisions contrary to public stockholder interests
risks.description: Initial stockholders own 20% of shares and can exert substantial influence over votes, potentially voting against public stockholder interests.
risks.why: Initial stockholders beneficially own 20% of outstanding common stock and may vote in any manner they choose on amendments, and they may purchase additional shares to increase control.

risks.risk_name: Inability to obtain additional financing may force restructuring or abandonment of business combination
risks.description: If cash from trust account is insufficient, we may be unable to secure additional financing needed to complete or fund the post-combination business.
risks.why: If the cash portion of the purchase price exceeds trust account funds net of redemptions, we may need additional financing, which may not be available on acceptable terms, if at all.

risks.risk_name: Resources wasted on unsuccessful business combination attempts may hinder future deals
risks.description: Costs incurred researching and negotiating failed business combinations may materially impair subsequent efforts to find and complete a deal.
risks.why: If we abandon a proposed business combination, costs for accountants, attorneys, and management time are likely unrecoverable, which could materially adversely affect subsequent attempts.

risks.risk_name: Key personnel may have conflicts of interest due to post-combination employment agreements
risks.description: Key personnel may negotiate employment terms with target businesses, creating conflicts in evaluating whether a combination is most advantageous.
risks.why: Key personnel may negotiate employment or consulting agreements with a target business in connection with a business combination, which may condition the deal on their retention or resignation.

risks.risk_name: Key personnel may not remain post-combination
risks.description: Key personnel may leave after the business combination if employment or consulting agreements cannot be negotiated.
risks.why: Retention of key personnel is contingent on negotiating agreements simultaneously with the business combination, and their resignation could be a condition to the deal, potentially disrupting leadership.

risks.risk_name: Inadequate assessment of target management
risks.description: The company may lack time, resources, or information to properly evaluate the target’s management capabilities.
risks.why: Limited due diligence may lead to incorrect assessments, resulting in a target whose management lacks skills to run a public company, harming post-combination operations and profitability.

risks.risk_name: Cross-border business combination risks
risks.description: Pursuing a target outside the U.S. introduces risks from foreign regulations, due diligence challenges, and currency fluctuations.
risks.why: Cross-border deals require navigating foreign government approvals, conducting due diligence in unfamiliar jurisdictions, and facing exchange rate volatility that can alter purchase price.

risks.risk_name: Substantial debt incurrence to complete combination
risks.description: Incurring significant debt to finance the business combination may strain financial condition and limit operational flexibility.
risks.why: Debt could accelerate repayment obligations upon covenant breaches, consume cash flow for interest/principal, restrict future borrowing, and reduce funds for corporate purposes.

risks.risk_name: Lack of diversification due to single business combination
risks.description: The company can complete only one business combination, making it dependent on a single business with limited products or services.
risks.why: With only $11,970,547 available from trust account and private placement proceeds, the company is restricted to one acquisition, creating concentration risk and limiting revenue streams.

risks.risk_name: Lack of diversification from completing initial business combination with a single target
risks.description: Focusing on one target business exposes the company to economic, competitive, and regulatory risks in a single industry without the ability to offset losses or spread risk.
risks.why: The company may not be able to combine with multiple targets due to complex accounting and SEC reporting requirements, leaving it undiversified and vulnerable to industry-specific adverse impacts.

risks.risk_name: Difficulty in completing simultaneous business combinations with multiple targets
risks.description: Attempting to acquire multiple targets at once may delay or prevent the initial business combination due to logistical and legal complexities.
risks.why: Each seller requires the closing of all deals to be contingent on one another, increasing negotiation burdens, due diligence costs, and risks of assimilating multiple operations.

risks.risk_name: Acquiring a private company with limited available information
risks.description: Making a business combination decision based on insufficient public data about a private target may lead to an unprofitable acquisition.
risks.why: Little public information exists about private companies, forcing the company to rely on limited data, which could result in choosing a target less profitable than expected.

risks.risk_name: Loss of key personnel post-combination impacting operations
risks.description: The success of the post-combination business depends on key personnel, whose departure could harm operations and profitability.
risks.why: Some key personnel may leave after the combination, and the company cannot guarantee their assessment of new management will be correct or that they understand SEC requirements.

risks.risk_name: Insufficient time commitment from officers and directors due to conflicts of interest
risks.description: Executives and directors allocate time to other businesses, reducing focus on identifying and completing a business combination.
risks.why: They are not required to commit specific hours to the company, serve on other boards, and may face conflicts in prioritizing this company’s search over other obligations.

risks.risk_name: Conflicts of interest in presenting business opportunities to other entities
risks.description: Officers and directors may be contractually obligated to present opportunities to other entities before offering them to the company.
risks.why: They have fiduciary duties to other entities, and the company has renounced interest in opportunities offered to them in other capacities, risking loss of potential targets.

risks.risk_name: Sponsor and management's financial interest in completing a deal may bias target selection
risks.description: Sponsor and executives stand to lose their entire investment if no business combination is completed, potentially influencing target selection.
risks.why: The Sponsor holds 4,312,500 founder shares and 4,850,000 private placement warrants worth nothing if the combination fails, creating pressure to complete any deal before the 18-month deadline.

risks.risk_name: Conflict of interest due to lack of prohibited financial interests
risks.description: Directors, officers, and affiliates may have financial interests in transactions involving the company, creating potential conflicts between their interests and those of stockholders.
risks.why: The company has no policy prohibiting such persons from having pecuniary interests in company transactions or engaging in competing business activities, which may influence their decisions on target selection and deal terms.

risks.risk_name: Potential business combination with affiliated entities
risks.description: The company may pursue a business combination with a target affiliated with the Sponsor, directors, or executive officers, despite not targeting such entities.
risks.why: Affiliates may compete for opportunities, and while independent director approval is required, conflicts of interest may still result in terms less advantageous to public stockholders.

risks.risk_name: Loss of control over target business post-combination
risks.description: After a business combination, the company may not maintain control of the target business due to share dilution or minority consolidation.
risks.why: Issuing substantial new shares in a transaction may reduce pre-transaction stockholders' ownership to a minority, and other minority holders may later combine shares to gain control.

risks.risk_name: Loss of target’s key personnel post-combination
risks.description: Key personnel of the target business may resign after the business combination, negatively impacting operations and profitability.
risks.why: The company cannot assure that management of the target will remain in place, and their departure could harm the post-combination business’s performance.

risks.risk_name: Risk of being classified as an investment company under the Investment Company Act
risks.description: The company may be deemed an investment company if it holds more than 40% of investment securities, triggering regulatory burdens or forced liquidation.
risks.why: If the trust account funds are not held solely in cash or permitted government securities, the company could exceed the 40% threshold, forcing compliance with burdensome rules or liquidation.

risks.risk_name: Reduced returns due to holding trust funds in cash instead of interest-bearing securities
risks.description: Holding trust account funds in cash to avoid investment company status reduces interest income, lowering funds available for redemption or liquidation.
risks.why: To mitigate investment company risk, funds were moved from U.S. government securities/money market funds to non-interest-bearing cash accounts, reducing potential returns to shareholders.

risks.risk_name: Failure to complete business combination within proposed SEC timeline
risks.description: Failure to complete a business combination within 24 months of IPO may trigger SEC scrutiny and risk of being deemed an investment company.
risks.why: The SEC’s proposed SPAC Rule Proposals require announcement within 18 months and completion within 24 months; failure to meet this may lead to classification as an investment company and forced liquidation.

risks.risk_name: Reduced interest income from trust account liquidation
risks.description: Funds in the trust account were moved from interest-bearing U.S. treasury obligations to cash, resulting in minimal or no interest income.
risks.why: After December 15, 2022, trust assets were liquidated and held in interest-bearing demand deposit accounts, which yield significantly less than prior U.S. treasury obligations or money market funds, reducing funds available for redemption or liquidation.

risks.risk_name: Nasdaq listing deficiency due to delayed annual meeting
risks.description: The company failed to hold an annual shareholder meeting within the required timeframe, triggering a Nasdaq listing deficiency.
risks.why: On January 9, 2023, Nasdaq notified the company of non-compliance with Listing Rule 5620(a), which requires an annual meeting no later than one year after the end of the 2021 fiscal year-end.

risks.risk_name: Nasdaq listing deficiency due to insufficient market value of listed securities
risks.description: The company’s Class A common stock market value fell below the $35 million minimum required for continued Nasdaq listing.
risks.why: For 30 consecutive business days prior to March 24, 2023, the MVLS of Class A common stock was below the $35 million threshold under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(b)(2).

risks.risk_name: Failure to meet Nasdaq initial listing requirements after business combination
risks.description: The company may not satisfy Nasdaq’s stricter initial listing requirements upon completing a business combination.
risks.why: Nasdaq requires a minimum $4.00 share price, $5.0 million stockholders’ equity, and 300 round lot holders (with 50% holding $2,500+ in value), which the company cannot guarantee it will meet.

risks.risk_name: Delisting from Nasdaq leading to OTC quotation
risks.description: If Nasdaq delists the company’s securities, they may only be quoted on an over-the-counter market.
risks.why: Nasdaq may delist the securities if compliance with listing rules is not regained by June 29, 2023 (annual meeting) or September 20, 2023 (MVLS), and no alternative exchange listing is secured.

risks.risk_name: Classification as a penny stock upon OTC quotation
risks.description: If securities trade OTC, they may be deemed penny stocks, triggering broker compliance burdens and reduced trading activity.
risks.why: OTC quotation could cause Class A common stock to be classified as a penny stock, requiring brokers to follow stricter rules, which may reduce secondary market trading activity.

risks.risk_name: Loss of covered securities status under federal preemption
risks.description: Loss of Nasdaq listing would subject the company to state securities regulation, unlike when listed on Nasdaq.
risks.why: Under the National Securities Markets Improvement Act, only Nasdaq-listed securities are covered securities exempt from state regulation; delisting removes this exemption, exposing the company to state-level oversight.

risks.risk_name: Dilution from future issuance of Class A common stock or preferred stock
risks.description: Issuance of additional shares for business combinations or employee plans may dilute existing shareholders’ interests.
risks.why: The company may issue up to 378,817,946 additional Class A shares or preferred stock, including upon conversion of founder shares at a ratio greater than one-to-one, diluting ownership and potentially changing control.

risks.risk_name: Change in control from issuance of additional shares
risks.description: Issuing a substantial number of new shares could result in a change of control, affecting NOL usage and management.
risks.why: A significant issuance of Class A common stock could trigger a change in control, potentially impairing the use of net operating loss carryforwards and leading to resignation or removal of current officers and directors.

risks.risk_name: Warrants may expire worthless if shares are not registered
risks.description: Warrants may be unexercisable for cash if the underlying shares are not registered under federal or state securities laws.
risks.why: The company has not registered the Class A common stock issuable upon warrant exercise; if registration is not completed within required timelines or fails, holders cannot exercise for cash and may be forced into cashless exercise or lose value.

risks.risk_name: Warrants unexercisable due to state securities law non-compliance
risks.description: Warrant holders may be unable to exercise if state securities law registration or exemption is unavailable.
risks.why: Warrants cannot be exercised for cash or cashless basis unless the issuance is registered or exempt under the securities laws of the holder’s state, which may not be available.

risks.risk_name: Cashless exercise of warrants may reduce shares received
risks.description: Holders may be required to exercise warrants on a cashless basis, resulting in fewer shares of Class A common stock than if exercised for cash.
risks.why: Cashless exercise calculates shares based on fair market value over 10 trading days, reducing the number received by the quotient of (exercise price differential) / (fair market value), as defined in the warrant agreement.

risks.risk_name: Warrants may be exercisable only on a cashless basis under certain conditions
risks.description: Warrants may be forced into cashless exercise if shares are not registered, not listed on a national exchange as covered securities, or upon redemption.
risks.why: The warrant agreement mandates cashless exercise under three conditions: (i) unregistered shares, (ii) shares not listed on exchange and qualify as covered securities under Section 18(b)(1), or (iii) upon redemption of public warrants.

risks.risk_name: Failure to register shares may prevent cash settlement of warrants
risks.description: The company is not required to net cash settle warrants or issue compensation if shares underlying warrants cannot be registered or qualified under securities laws.
risks.why: The company explicitly states it will never be required to net cash settle warrants or provide alternative compensation if registration or state qualification is unavailable.

risks.risk_name: Registration rights of initial stockholders may depress stock price and hinder business combination
risks.description: Registration of large volumes of shares held by initial stockholders and affiliates may negatively impact market price and complicate business combination negotiations.
risks.why: Registration of founder shares, private placement warrants, and working capital loan conversions could flood the market, lowering share price and causing target companies to demand higher equity or cash consideration.

risks.risk_name: Initial stockholders receive disproportionate shares upon business combination
risks.description: Initial stockholders receive 20% of post-combination shares regardless of additional issuances, unlike other SPACs that cap at pre-combination totals.
risks.why: Founder shares convert to 20% of total outstanding shares after business combination, including all new issuances (except seller shares and private placement warrants), increasing dilution to public shareholders.

risks.risk_name: Material agreements may be amended without stockholder approval
risks.description: Key agreements like the underwriting and letter agreements can be amended by board approval alone, potentially harming public shareholders.
risks.why: Amendments to lock-up provisions, registration rights, or other material terms require only board consent and applicable party approval, not stockholder vote, and may facilitate deals adverse to public investors.

risks.risk_name: Warrant terms may be amended adversely with 50% holder approval
risks.description: The company can alter warrant terms—such as exercise price, duration, or shares per warrant—with approval of only 50% of public warrant holders.
risks.why: The warrant agreement permits amendments that reduce shares per warrant, increase exercise price, or shorten exercise period if approved by holders of at least 50% of public warrants, without individual consent.

risks.risk_name: Exclusive forum clause limits legal recourse for warrant holders
risks.description: Warrant holders must litigate disputes in New York courts, potentially increasing costs and limiting access to favorable jurisdictions.
risks.why: The warrant agreement mandates exclusive jurisdiction in New York state or federal courts for all warrant-related claims, requiring holders to pursue litigation in a single, potentially inconvenient forum.

risks.risk_name: Warrant exercise price and redemption trigger price adjustments
risks.description: Warrant exercise price and redemption trigger price may be adjusted downward if certain conditions are met, potentially reducing warrant value.
risks.why: If new shares or equity-linked securities are issued below $9.20 per share, exceed 60% of total equity proceeds, and the 20-day post-combination VWAP is below $9.20, the exercise price becomes 115% of the higher of Market Value or Newly Issued Price, and redemption trigger becomes 180% of that value, lowering potential upside.

risks.risk_name: Warrant redemption forcing unfavorable holder actions
risks.description: The company may redeem warrants even if holders cannot exercise them, forcing holders to exercise at a disadvantage, sell at market price, or accept nominal redemption value.
risks.why: Redemption can occur if stock price equals or exceeds $18.00 for 20 of 30 trading days, even if registration for underlying shares is not possible under state laws, leaving holders with no choice but to exercise, sell, or accept low redemption value.

risks.risk_name: Dilution from warrant exercises reducing value of shares issued in business combination
risks.description: Exercise of warrants increases shares outstanding, diluting equity and reducing the value of shares issued to complete a business combination.
risks.why: Warrants for 8,625,000 public shares and 4,850,000 private placement shares (plus up to 1,500,000 more from loans) could be exercised, increasing share count and lowering the value of shares issued to target businesses, making acquisitions more costly.

risks.risk_name: Unit structure reducing investor appeal due to fractional warrant handling
risks.description: Units contain only half a warrant, and fractional shares are rounded down, making units less valuable than those with full warrants.
risks.why: Each unit contains one-half of one public warrant, no fractional warrants are issued, and any fractional share upon exercise is rounded down, unlike competitors whose units include whole warrants, potentially reducing perceived value.

risks.risk_name: Anti-takeover provisions deterring premium acquisition offers
risks.description: Provisions like staggered board and preferred stock issuance may prevent hostile takeovers, limiting investor upside potential.
risks.why: Amended certificate includes staggered board, board authority to issue preferred stock, and Delaware anti-takeover laws, which together make removal of management harder and discourage premium takeover bids.

risks.risk_name: Exclusive Delaware forum provision limiting litigation options
risks.description: Mandatory litigation in Delaware courts may discourage lawsuits and limit stockholders' ability to seek favorable judicial forums.
risks.why: Certificate requires all covered claims (fiduciary duty, DGCL, internal affairs) to be brought only in Delaware Court of Chancery, which may discourage suits and prevent stockholders from choosing more favorable jurisdictions.

risks.risk_name: Lack of operating history impairs ability to evaluate business prospects
risks.description: As a blank check company with no operating results, investors have no basis to assess ability to complete a business combination.
risks.why: The company has no operating history, generates no revenues until a business combination, and past performance of management is not indicative of future success, leaving investors without a basis to evaluate prospects.

risks.risk_name: Cyber incidents targeting the company or future business combination partners
risks.description: Cyberattacks on the company or travel-focused target businesses could cause data loss, operational disruption, or financial harm.
risks.why: The company lacks significant cybersecurity investments and targets travel businesses that handle large volumes of sensitive customer data, making them vulnerable to breaches that could damage operations, reputation, or finances.

risks.risk_name: Changes in laws or regulations or failure to comply
risks.description: Changes in laws or failure to comply with SEC and other regulations may adversely affect business operations and ability to complete an initial business combination.
risks.why: Compliance is costly and complex; laws and their interpretation change over time, and non-compliance could materially impact business, investments, and results of operations.

risks.risk_name: Reliance on emerging growth company exemptions
risks.description: Using exemptions available to emerging growth companies may make securities less attractive to investors and reduce comparability with other public companies.
risks.why: Exemptions include reduced disclosures on executive compensation, no Section 404 auditor attestation, and opting out of advisory votes, which may lead to lower investor confidence and stock price volatility.

risks.risk_name: Use of extended transition period for accounting standards
risks.description: Adopting new accounting standards at the same time as private companies may make financial statement comparisons with other public companies difficult or impossible.
risks.why: As an emerging growth company, Global Gas Corp elected not to opt out of the extended transition period, creating potential mismatches in accounting standards used versus non-exempt public companies.

risks.risk_name: Reduced disclosure as a smaller reporting company
risks.description: Reduced disclosure obligations as a smaller reporting company may hinder comparability of financial statements with other public companies.
risks.why: The company may provide only two years of audited financial statements and benefit from other reduced disclosures, which limits investor ability to compare performance with full-reporting companies.

risks.risk_name: Fluctuations in derivative liability fair value
risks.description: Recurring fair value remeasurement of warrant derivatives causes volatile non-cash gains/losses that may adversely affect earnings and stock price.
risks.why: ASC 815 requires quarterly remeasurement of derivative liabilities, leading to material non-cash gains or losses based on uncontrollable market factors, potentially impacting investor perception and deal attractiveness.

risks.risk_name: Material weakness in internal control over financial reporting
risks.description: A material weakness in accounting for extinguishment of a contingent obligation compromises accurate and timely financial reporting.
risks.why: This weakness caused restatement of Q2 and Q3 2022 financials and could lead to future misstatements, regulatory sanctions, or loss of investor confidence if not fully remediated.

risks.risk_name: Potential litigation from prior financial restatements
risks.description: Past financial restatements due to internal control weaknesses expose the company to future litigation under securities or contractual laws.
risks.why: The restatement of interim financials for 2022 creates exposure to claims under federal/state securities laws or contractual disputes, which could materially harm business and financial condition even if unfounded.

risks.risk_name: Failure to achieve expected performance benefits of Lightbridge Fuel™
risks.description: Lightbridge Fuel™ may not deliver projected economic and safety benefits over traditional nuclear fuel, such as higher burnup, power density, or uprate capabilities.
risks.why: The company projects significant improvements in burnup and power density, but conventional oxide fuel is nearing its design limits, and Lightbridge Fuel™ has not yet been commercially proven or tested at scale beyond R&D with DOE labs.

risks.risk_name: Delays or failures in third-party testing and regulatory approval
risks.description: Lightbridge Fuel™ may face delays or failures in testing through third parties or DOE national labs, or in obtaining regulatory approval for deployment.
risks.why: The company is currently performing most R&D with DOE national labs and anticipates testing via third parties, but no commercial deployment has occurred, and regulatory pathways for novel metallic fuel are unproven.

risks.risk_name: Reliance on unproven SMR deployment timelines
risks.description: The economic case for Lightbridge Fuel™ depends on SMRs beginning operations as early as 2029, which may be delayed or fail to materialize.
risks.why: The company expects Lightbridge Fuel™ to benefit SMRs starting as early as 2029, but SMRs are still in development and licensing phases with no guaranteed commercial deployment schedule.

risks.risk_name: Failure to secure sufficient funding or partnerships for R&D
risks.description: Continued development of Lightbridge Fuel™ depends on ongoing R&D with DOE labs and third parties, which may not be sustained.
risks.why: The company currently relies primarily on DOE national labs for R&D and has not disclosed secured long-term funding or partnerships beyond current activities, creating dependency risk.

risks.risk_name: Market adoption risk due to entrenched conventional fuel use
risks.description: Nuclear utilities may resist switching from established oxide fuels to Lightbridge Fuel™ despite projected benefits.
risks.why: Conventional oxide fuel is currently used in 70% of global operating reactors, and utilities are constrained by existing licensing and operational frameworks that favor proven technologies.

risks.risk_name: Limited power uprate potential in existing large reactors
risks.description: Existing large pressurized water reactors can only realize up to a 17% power uprate with Lightbridge Fuel™, falling short of the potential 30% due to design limitations.
risks.why: The text states that existing large PWRs are not designed to handle a 30% power increase, and the maximum achievable is estimated at approximately 17%, limiting economic benefits.

risks.risk_name: Limited number of new large reactors to be built
risks.description: Only a limited number of new large reactors may be constructed, reducing the market for Lightbridge Fuel™'s full 30% power uprate potential.
risks.why: The passage explicitly states that only a limited number of new, large reactors will be built, meaning most of the fuel's potential benefit cannot be captured in this segment.

risks.risk_name: Delayed or cancelled nuclear programs post-Fukushima
risks.description: Public concern after Fukushima led to slowdowns or halts in nuclear construction and early shutdowns, shrinking the projected global nuclear market.
risks.why: The Fukushima accident increased public concerns, resulting in delayed/cancelled nuclear programs and reduced market projections for 2025-2030, per WNA reference cases.

risks.risk_name: Supply chain risk for HALEU fuel
risks.description: Dependence on HALEU supply chain development poses risk to commercial deployment of Lightbridge Fuel™.
risks.why: Lightbridge joined the DOE’s HALEU Consortium to mitigate HALEU supply risk, indicating that reliable access to HALEU is uncertain and critical for deployment.

risks.risk_name: Uncertainty in funding and timeline for DOE-supported testing
risks.description: Reliance on DOE-funded testing at INL and MIT introduces risk due to unquantified financial benefit and multi-year timelines.
risks.why: While agreements exist for irradiation testing and MIT studies, the financial benefit to Lightbridge from the $800K DOE grant to MIT cannot be quantified, and work spans years.

risks.risk_name: Funding constraints limiting fuel development timelines
risks.description: Lightbridge lacks sufficient funding to sustain its nuclear fuel development program at the level required to meet projected timelines.
risks.why: The company states its ability to fund fuel development is severely limited due to funding constraints, in addition to corporate overhead, making government funding essential for success.

risks.risk_name: Limited access to irradiation test loops at ATR
risks.description: Restricted availability of test loops in the ATR at INL may prevent sufficient irradiation data for regulatory approval of Lightbridge Fuel™.
risks.why: Irradiation test loop capacity in the ATR is limited and highly competitive, potentially requiring an additional LTR testing step in commercial reactors before LTA testing can occur.

risks.risk_name: Need for additional LTR testing due to insufficient ATR data
risks.description: Without increased ATR test loop capacity, Lightbridge may need to conduct LTR testing in commercial reactors before LTA testing, delaying commercialization.
risks.why: If ATR loop testing cannot provide sufficient data, an extra fuel development step of LTR testing in a large commercial PWR will be necessary, extending timelines by 15–20 years.

risks.risk_name: Unproven fabrication process for full-length metallic fuel rods
risks.description: Fabrication of full-length (12–14 ft) metallic fuel rods for PWRs has not yet been demonstrated with enriched uranium.
risks.why: While surrogate materials were co-extruded in 2021, actual fuel rods with enriched uranium at full length have not been fabricated, and pilot-scale facility FEED study is only planned for 2023.

risks.risk_name: Lack of experimental data on metallic fuel performance
risks.description: There is insufficient publicly available experimental data on Lightbridge’s metallic fuel under normal and off-normal reactor conditions.
risks.why: Irradiation experiments are essential to confirm fuel performance, and current data gaps require extensive testing to support regulatory approval and model validation.

risks.risk_name: Inadequacy of existing analytical models for metallic fuel
risks.description: Current analytical models may not accurately predict the behavior of Lightbridge’s metallic fuel during normal or off-normal reactor events.
risks.why: Experimental data from planned irradiation tests will be needed to identify where new or modified models are required, introducing uncertainty in fuel performance predictions.

risks.risk_name: Infrastructure not licensed for high-assay low-enriched uranium metal fuel
risks.description: Existing nuclear infrastructure is licensed only for uranium oxide up to 5% enrichment, not for Lightbridge’s 19.75% enriched uranium metal fuel.
risks.why: Conversion, enrichment, fabrication, storage, and shipping facilities must undergo regulatory licensing to handle uranium metal enriched up to 19.75%, which has not yet been done.

risks.risk_name: Uncertainty in securing LTA agreements with nuclear utilities
risks.description: Lightbridge must secure engagement with a utility willing to accept its lead test assemblies in commercial reactors, which requires regulatory licensing by others.
risks.why: In the U.S., the fuel fabricator and utility are primarily responsible for securing regulatory approvals for LTA operation, which are outside Lightbridge’s direct control.

risks.risk_name: Delayed commercialization due to long development timeline
risks.description: Commercialization of Lightbridge Fuel™ is projected to take 15–20 years before first purchase orders, with deployment two years later.
risks.why: Based on current funding and test access constraints, the company expects first fuel reload orders in the 2040s and deployment in commercial reactors only after that.

risks.risk_name: Reliance on U.S. government funding for program viability
risks.description: Lightbridge’s fuel development and commercialization depend on securing significant U.S. government funding, which is not guaranteed.
risks.why: The company explicitly states that seeking and securing significant government funding is essential for success, given its inability to fund development independently.

risks.risk_name: Competition from Accident Tolerant Fuels (ATF) extending cycle length to 24 months
risks.description: ATF vendors may successfully extend fuel cycle length to 24 months using higher enrichments, undermining Lightbridge Fuel™'s key economic value proposition.
risks.why: ATF vendors are shifting focus from safety to cycle extension by increasing enrichment from 5% to 7-8%, directly competing with Lightbridge's core advantage of enabling 18-to-24-month cycles in existing PWRs, which could severely weaken its economic value proposition.

risks.risk_name: Limited availability of uranium metal enriched to 19.75%
risks.description: Uranium metal enriched to 19.75% is currently available only in small quantities for research, hindering commercial deployment of Lightbridge Fuel™.
risks.why: Deployment requires enrichment levels up to 19.75%, but such material is currently limited to small quantities sufficient only for research and testing, creating a critical supply bottleneck for commercialization.

risks.risk_name: Need for commercial-scale de-conversion/metallization and licensed shipping containers
risks.description: Commercial deployment requires unproven infrastructure for de-conversion, metallization, and shipping containers for high-enriched uranium metal fuel.
risks.why: Lightbridge Fuel™ requires deployment of de-conversion/metallization capability at commercial scale and design/licensing of shipping containers for fuel assemblies enriched up to 19.75%, neither of which currently exist at commercial scale.

risks.risk_name: Dependence on substantial U.S. government funding for R&D
risks.description: Without significant U.S. government funding and cost-sharing, Lightbridge cannot feasibly fund its next-generation fuel development alone.
risks.why: Long development timelines and high R&D costs make it unfeasible for the Company to fund future fuel development efforts on its own without substantial U.S. government funding and cost-sharing contributions.

risks.risk_name: Export control regulatory delays and denials
risks.description: Export of technology or collaboration with foreign entities requires government authorizations that may be delayed or denied, impacting international business.
risks.why: Export of services/technology is subject to 10 C.F.R. Part 810 and Part 110, and delays or denials in obtaining required governmental authorizations could materially affect international business and fuel development timelines.

risks.risk_name: Regulatory approvals for testing and fabrication require third-party compliance
risks.description: Third parties must obtain regulatory approvals for testing and fabricating Lightbridge Fuel™, and failure could delay or block commercialization.
risks.why: Testing facilities and fuel fabricators must obtain approvals from host country nuclear regulators and NRC, and responsibility for compliance lies with contractors and licensees, not Lightbridge, creating execution risk.

risks.risk_name: Competition from cheaper electricity sources like natural gas and renewables
risks.description: Declining demand for nuclear power due to cheaper alternatives like natural gas and renewables could reduce market for Lightbridge Fuel™.
risks.why: Natural gas has been the cheapest U.S. power option in recent years, causing utilities to abandon nuclear initiatives, and renewables are perceived as safer, reducing potential demand for nuclear fuel technology.

risks.risk_name: Patent expiration starting in 2027 reducing competitive advantage
risks.description: Core U.S. patents for Lightbridge Fuel™ begin expiring in 2027, potentially eroding proprietary protection and competitive advantage.
risks.why: U.S. patents held by Lightbridge begin expiring in 2027 (unless divisional), and without ongoing patent protection, competitors could replicate the technology, diminishing its market exclusivity.

risks.risk_name: Inability to raise sufficient additional capital
risks.description: The company may be unable to raise the hundreds of millions of dollars needed to fund R&D and operations through commercialization of its nuclear fuel.
risks.why: As of Dec 31, 2022, the company had $28.9M in cash and an accumulated deficit of $144.5M; it requires up to several hundred million dollars more, and capital may not be available on acceptable terms or at all.

risks.risk_name: Dilution of shareholders from equity financing
risks.description: Raising capital through equity offerings will cause significant dilution to existing shareholders.
risks.why: Issuing equity securities to raise funds will dilute current stockholders, and sales of substantial amounts of common stock may cause the trading price to decline.

risks.risk_name: Restrictive covenants from debt financing
risks.description: Debt financing could impose covenants that limit operational flexibility, such as incurring more debt or making capital expenditures.
risks.why: Debt financing may involve agreements with covenants restricting specific actions like incurring additional debt, making capital expenditures, or declaring dividends.

risks.risk_name: Unfavorable terms in new financing
risks.description: New equity or debt financing may include terms that are not favorable to the company or its stockholders, such as liquidation preferences.
risks.why: Any new financing may contain terms like liquidation and other preferences that are not favorable to the company or its stockholders.

risks.risk_name: Reliance on uncertain U.S. government funding
risks.description: The company's fuel development timeline and funding depend heavily on unpredictable U.S. government R&D funding.
risks.why: Government funding is subject to political processes, budgetary limitations, congressional appropriations, and policy changes, including under the Biden administration and future administrations.

risks.risk_name: Termination or modification of agreements with U.S. national laboratories
risks.description: Loss or change in agreements with U.S. national laboratories and DOE could impair R&D and commercialization of nuclear fuel.
risks.why: Agreements with national laboratories are subject to DOE review and approval; termination, expiration, or modification could adversely affect fuel development and deployment.

risks.risk_name: Disruption from COVID-19 or other pathogens at national labs
risks.description: Outbreaks of COVID-19 or other pathogens could disrupt operations at U.S. national laboratories critical to the company's R&D.
risks.why: A COVID-19 outbreak, including variant strains or other pathogens, may affect future operations of the U.S. national laboratories.

risks.risk_name: Delays or cost overruns in fuel development
risks.description: Delays in achieving milestones or regulatory licensing could cause significant delays and cost overruns in fuel development.
risks.why: Any shortfall in R&D funding, delay in milestones, or uncertainty in regulatory timelines could result in significant delays and cost overruns.

risks.risk_name: Inaccurate economic models for fuel profitability
risks.description: The company's economic models predicting payback to utilities may be inaccurate, undermining customer adoption.
risks.why: The preliminary economic model is based on assumptions that may not prove accurate; for example, if ATF extends cycle lengths to 24 months, it could undermine the economic value of the company's fuel.

risks.risk_name: Unproven economic viability for SMRs
risks.description: The economic model for small modular reactors (SMRs) is undeveloped and depends on unpredictable factors like power prices and uranium metallization costs.
risks.why: SMR economic viability depends on favorable wholesale power prices, upfront capital investment for 30% power uprate, and unpredictable costs of uranium metallization and commercial-scale fabrication.

risks.risk_name: Uncertainty of fuel suitability for CANDU reactors
risks.description: The company has not confirmed whether its metallic fuel is suitable for CANDU reactors and lacks an economic model for them.
risks.why: No feasibility study has been conducted to confirm fuel suitability for CANDU reactors, so potential economic benefits are unknown.

risks.risk_name: Failure to secure a strategic business combination partner
risks.description: Failure to find a strategic partner could adversely affect the company's business and financial condition.
risks.why: A failure to find a strategic alternative, such as a potential business combination partner, would adversely affect the business, financial condition, and results of operations and may result in company failure.

risks.risk_name: Loss of Halden research reactor for fuel testing
risks.description: The Halden research reactor, used for testing fuel designs, was shut down in June 2018 and will not reopen, delaying regulatory licensing.
risks.why: The company relied on Halden for irradiation data to support regulatory licensing of its LTA operation; alternative test facilities may not be available or may cause significant delays.

risks.risk_name: Insufficient irradiation testing capacity at ATR
risks.description: The ATR at INL has only one available flow loop for fuel rod irradiation, limiting data generation for regulatory approval.
risks.why: With only one loop available, the ATR cannot accommodate sufficient fuel rod testing to justify regulatory approval for LTA in a commercial PWR without adding new loops.

risks.risk_name: Uncertainty of U.S. government funding for reactor operations
risks.description: Funding for U.S. research reactors like ATR depends on congressional appropriations and government priorities, which are uncertain.
risks.why: Funding for reactor improvements or continued operations is not assured and is subject to external political and budgetary decisions beyond the company's control.

risks.risk_name: Lack of commercial reactor testing history for fuel designs
risks.description: The company's fuel designs have never been tested in a commercial reactor, making actual performance and adoption uncertain.
risks.why: Without real-world commercial reactor data, the fuel's ability to deliver expected benefits like power uprate or longer cycles cannot be confirmed.

risks.risk_name: Non-uniform heat flux in metallic fuel design
risks.description: The helical multi-lobe shape of the metallic fuel may cause non-uniform heat flux, potentially reducing critical heat flux and limiting power uprate.
risks.why: The design's geometry, while improving cooling, may create thermal hotspots that adversely impact safety margins and performance capabilities.

risks.risk_name: Unproven fabrication of full-length metallic fuel rods
risks.description: Co-extrusion fabrication of full-length PWR metallic fuel rods has not been sufficiently demonstrated for commercial use.
risks.why: Current fabrication methods have only produced small-scale rods; scaling to 12–14 foot lengths for commercial reactors remains unproven.

risks.risk_name: Lack of commercial agreements with fuel fabricators
risks.description: Failure to secure commercial arrangements with fuel fabricators could prevent market entry for the company's metallic fuel.
risks.why: Without partnerships with existing fabricators, the company cannot produce, supply, or commercialize its fuel technology, risking business failure.

risks.risk_name: Infrastructure incompatibility with high-enrichment metallic uranium
risks.description: Existing nuclear infrastructure is licensed only for low-enriched uranium oxide, not for 19.75% enriched uranium metal.
risks.why: Facilities for conversion, enrichment, fabrication, storage, and shipping are not licensed or designed to handle uranium metal enriched up to 19.75%.

risks.risk_name: Regulatory delays due to novel fuel design
risks.description: The novelty of the fuel design will trigger extended NRC and global regulatory reviews, delaying commercialization.
risks.why: Regulators may require additional data or testing beyond what is standard for existing fuels, leading to unplanned delays and increased R&D costs.

risks.risk_name: Public and political opposition to nuclear power
risks.description: Public opposition to nuclear power, exacerbated by Fukushima, may delay or block regulatory approvals and new plant construction.
risks.why: Fukushima increased opposition globally, leading to canceled programs and public hearings that can delay or deny licensing for new fuels like Lightbridge's.

risks.risk_name: High cost of commercial-scale fuel production
risks.description: Producing metallic fuel at $5,000–$10,000/kg may not be economically viable without major cost reductions.
risks.why: Further cost reduction requires a $B+ government-funded R&D program over 15–20 years, with no guarantee of success or funding.

risks.risk_name: Supply chain dependency on outside material suppliers
risks.description: Fuel fabrication depends on external suppliers for nuclear and other materials, whose disruptions could halt production.
risks.why: Any difficulty by fabricators in obtaining required materials could prevent the company from eventually marketing its fuel technology.

risks.risk_name: No commercial supply of HALEU available in the U.S.
risks.description: Our fuel designs require HALEU (5-19.75% U-235) in metallic form, but no commercial supply exists in the U.S., and only limited quantities are available from the DOE.
risks.why: HALEU is essential for our fuel assemblies, and without reliable commercial sourcing, fuel fabricators cannot produce our products, directly blocking commercialization.

risks.risk_name: Difficulty obtaining regulated materials like zirconium or its alloys
risks.description: Fuel fabricators need zirconium or its alloys for components, but these materials are regulated and may be difficult to obtain or have unfavorable pricing.
risks.why: Supply constraints or high costs for these regulated materials could prevent fabricators from producing fuel based on our technology, impairing marketability.

risks.risk_name: Global shipping delays and inflationary cost pressures
risks.description: Worldwide shipping delays and historically high material/equipment prices due to inflation and transportation complexities may disrupt our supply chain.
risks.why: These disruptions could delay development of our nuclear fuel technology and impact our R&D timeline and financial results if they persist.

risks.risk_name: Supply chain disruptions from third-party vendor issues
risks.description: Third-party vendors may face labor shortages, facility closures, port disruptions, or travel restrictions, impacting our supply chain.
risks.why: Such disruptions could delay development of our nuclear fuel technology and hinder execution of our R&D strategy, affecting financial performance.

risks.risk_name: Falling prices of non-nuclear energy sources
risks.description: If prices of non-nuclear energy sources fall due to policy or market forces, it could reduce demand for new nuclear power plants.
risks.why: This would shrink the potential market for our nuclear fuel technology, especially in markets where energy economics drive new plant decisions.

risks.risk_name: Government subsidies for renewable energy creating indirect competition
risks.description: Government subsidies and incentives for renewables like wind and solar may make them more attractive than nuclear power, reducing demand for our products.
risks.why: These subsidies could cause customers to choose renewables over nuclear, or competitors to leverage them to develop more attractive alternatives to our technology.

risks.risk_name: Loss of key senior management or inability to retain skilled personnel
risks.description: Our success depends on senior management and skilled nuclear engineers; losing them or failing to attract replacements could delay commercialization.
risks.why: Mr. Grae, Dr. Mushakov, and Mr. Goldman possess critical industry knowledge and networks; a recent senior engineer resignation and difficulty replacing them on comparable terms highlight this vulnerability.

risks.risk_name: Inability to recruit and retain qualified engineers and scientists
risks.description: Intense competition for skilled nuclear professionals may prevent us from hiring or retaining the personnel needed to develop and commercialize our technology.
risks.why: The nuclear industry's recent resurgence has intensified competition, and failure to secure key competencies could directly impair our R&D and business operations.

risks.risk_name: Export control regulations limiting international sales
risks.description: Exporting our technology internationally requires governmental authorizations, which may be denied or delayed, restricting revenue growth.
risks.why: Without export approvals, we cannot sell abroad; violations could result in fines or multi-year export bans, severely hindering international expansion.

risks.risk_name: Competition from other nuclear fuel designs, including ATFs
risks.description: Other companies are developing advanced nuclear fuels (e.g., ATFs) that may extend reactor cycle lengths, undermining our economic value proposition.
risks.why: Some competitors have long-term utility contracts and greater resources; if ATFs prove viable for 24-month cycles, our fuel’s competitive advantage could be erased.

risks.risk_name: DOE asserting ownership over inventions in our PCT patents
risks.description: The DOE may claim ownership of inventions in our 2007/2008 PCT patents if they were conceived or reduced to practice under a DOE contract.
risks.why: Work on subject matter in these patents was done under a DOE contract; if a U.S. court agrees with the DOE’s claim, our intellectual property rights could be compromised.

risks.risk_name: Patent infringement claims
risks.description: Third parties may claim our nuclear fuel designs infringe their patents, leading to costly litigation, injunctions, or forced licensing.
risks.why: We may not hold licenses for third-party patents, and infringement suits could force us to stop commercialization, pay damages, or seek nonexclusive licenses that competitors can also access.

risks.risk_name: Patent litigation and interference proceedings
risks.description: We may face costly patent litigation or USPTO interference proceedings, even if resolved in our favor, diverting management time and resources.
risks.why: Such proceedings are expensive, competitors may have greater financial resources to sustain them, and uncertainties could harm our ability to compete.

risks.risk_name: Cybersecurity breaches and data loss
risks.description: Security breaches on our systems or third-party networks may lead to unauthorized access, loss, or exposure of confidential and customer data.
risks.why: Despite security measures, threats like hacking, malware, insider errors, or state-sponsored attacks can bypass defenses, and insurance may not cover resulting losses.

risks.risk_name: Technological obsolescence
risks.description: Failure to advance our fuel technologies may render them uncompetitive or obsolete compared to alternatives in development by others.
risks.why: Competitors may develop lower-cost or higher-performance technologies, and we may be unable to secure funding for necessary R&D to keep pace.

risks.risk_name: Acquisition integration and performance risks
risks.description: Acquisitions may fail to deliver expected benefits due to integration failures, unmet expectations, or dilution from equity/debt issuance.
risks.why: We may incur costs identifying acquisitions, fail to integrate personnel or technologies, allocate purchase price to goodwill that may later be impaired, or issue dilutive securities.

risks.risk_name: Inadequate intellectual property protection
risks.description: Our patents may not issue, may be invalidated, or may not provide sufficient coverage to prevent competitors from replicating our technology.
