risks.why: Pending applications may not grant, issued patents can be challenged or circumvented, and patent laws or interpretations may change, reducing protection scope.

risks.risk_name: Loss of Russian and Eurasian patent protection due to sanctions
risks.description: U.S. sanctions may prevent payment of patent annuities to Russian and Eurasian patent offices, risking loss of patent rights in those jurisdictions.
risks.why: Payments must go through the sanctioned Russian Central Bank; although a temporary OFAC license exists, its permanence is uncertain, and non-payment could invalidate patents.

risks.risk_name: Weakened intellectual property enforcement in Russia
risks.description: Russia’s decree allows unsanctioned use of foreign-owned patents without compensation, undermining protection for our Russian patents.
risks.why: The March 2022 Russian decree permits use of foreign patents without renumeration for entities from countries deemed 'unfriendly,' creating legal uncertainty.

risks.risk_name: Failure to timely file or maintain patents
risks.description: We may fail to file patents on key technologies in time, or at all, leaving innovations unprotected and vulnerable to replication.
risks.why: We may overlook filing opportunities, and even if filed, patents may not be broad enough to block competitors from developing similar technologies.

risks.risk_name: Trade secret misappropriation or leakage
risks.description: Trade secrets may be lost through employee or third-party breaches, leaving us without legal recourse if competitors independently develop the same technology.
risks.why: Agreements with employees and consultants may be violated, enforcement is costly and uncertain, and courts outside the U.S. often offer weaker trade secret protection.

risks.risk_name: Russian intellectual property laws may impair our rights
risks.description: Russian laws, including those enacted in response to sanctions, may deny renumeration for our patents and limit our ability to enforce IP rights developed in Russia.
risks.why: A March 2022 Russian decree allows unsanctioned use of patents from 'unfriendly' foreign states without renumeration, and Russian IP laws may not adequately protect our earlier patent filings originating there.

risks.risk_name: Foreign jurisdictions may inadequately protect our intellectual property
risks.description: Laws in certain foreign countries, especially developing ones, do not enforce patents as effectively as U.S. law, making it difficult to stop infringement.
risks.why: Legal systems in some countries do not favor patent enforcement, and defending our rights abroad could lead to substantial costs and divert management attention.

risks.risk_name: Material weakness in internal control over financial reporting
risks.description: A material weakness in recording accounts payable invoices was identified, risking inaccurate or untimely financial reporting.
risks.why: Management concluded as of December 31, 2022, that internal controls were ineffective due to this specific weakness, which could impair financial reporting accuracy and investor confidence.

risks.risk_name: Issuance of preferred stock may dilute common stockholders' rights
risks.description: The company can issue preferred stock with superior rights, potentially diluting common stock value and altering voting or distribution priorities.
risks.why: Preferred stock may rank ahead of common stock in dividends and liquidation, have greater voting rights, and include conversion features that dilute common shares without shareholder approval.

risks.risk_name: Stock price volatility may negatively affect investor returns
risks.description: Market fluctuations unrelated to company performance may cause our stock price to fall, making it difficult for shareholders to sell at or above purchase price.
risks.why: The stock market may experience extreme volatility that is unrelated to our performance, which could cause our stock price to decline regardless of our results.

risks.risk_name: Delisting from Nasdaq Capital Market would impair liquidity and capital raising
risks.description: Failure to meet Nasdaq listing requirements could lead to delisting, reducing trading liquidity and hindering future capital raises.
risks.why: Delisting would substantially decrease trading, lower market liquidity, and prevent use of Form S-3 for offerings, impairing our ability to raise capital through at-the-market or other offerings.

risks.risk_name: Issuance of additional common or convertible securities may dilute existing shareholders
risks.description: Issuing more common stock or convertible securities could significantly dilute existing shareholders' ownership and lower stock price.
risks.why: The company is authorized to issue up to 25M common shares and 10M preferred shares, and may issue additional shares for financings, acquisitions, or incentive plans, causing dilution.

risks.risk_name: Net operating loss (NOL) utilization is limited by Section 382 ownership changes
risks.description: Our ability to use NOLs is restricted due to prior ownership changes and potential future changes under Section 382 of the Internal Revenue Code.
risks.why: Prior ownership changes have already limited pre-2018 NOLs, and future changes — some beyond our control — could further restrict NOL use, especially if profitability is not achieved.

risks.risk_name: Shareholder activism may divert management focus and increase costs
risks.description: Activist shareholder campaigns could impose significant costs and distract management from business operations.
risks.why: Activism may lead to substantial expenses for advisors, create uncertainty, harm employee retention, and cause stock price fluctuations unrelated to company performance.

risks.risk_name: Economic downturns reducing demand for products and increasing costs
risks.description: Weak global or regional economic conditions can reduce customer demand for our products and increase costs due to inflation, raw material price volatility, and supply chain disruptions.
risks.why: Declining consumer/business confidence, volatile raw material prices, high unemployment, and fluctuating exchange rates have historically reduced demand and increased costs; customers may delay purchases, reduce inventory, or default on obligations.

risks.risk_name: Dependence on cyclical industries with declining demand
risks.description: Our sales are tied to cyclical industries like metalcasting, paper, and construction, which face declining demand, mill closures, and reduced capital expenditures during economic slowdowns.
risks.why: Metalcasting demand depends on automotive and equipment markets sensitive to recessions; North American/European paper production is declining, leading to mill closures; construction markets reduce spending during downturns.

risks.risk_name: Loss of key PCC contracts with paper mills
risks.description: Failure of paper mills to renew long-term PCC supply agreements could significantly reduce sales and trigger asset impairments.
risks.why: Paper PCC sales were $381.7M in 2022 (18% of net sales) under long-term evergreen contracts; non-renewal or less favorable terms could directly reduce revenue and impair satellite plant assets.

risks.risk_name: Increased competitive pressure lowering profit margins
risks.description: Competition from larger rivals and lower-cost producers pressures pricing, reduces margins, and threatens market share.
risks.why: Some competitors have greater financial resources and flexibility; competition from China and India increases price pressure; consolidations in customer industries concentrate purchasing power to extract lower prices.

risks.risk_name: High debt levels and interest rate volatility impairing financial flexibility
risks.description: Significant debt obligations and rising interest rates strain cash flow and limit ability to fund operations or respond to market changes.
risks.why: At Dec 31, 2022, total debt was $1,070.1M; SOFR-based interest rates increase expense with rate hikes; cash flow must cover interest payments, reducing flexibility for capex or working capital.

risks.risk_name: Breach of debt covenants triggering default and acceleration of debt
risks.description: Failure to meet financial covenants in debt agreements could result in immediate repayment demands and asset insufficiency to cover obligations.
risks.why: Covenants include maximum net leverage and minimum interest coverage ratios; breach allows lenders to declare all debt immediately due, and assets may not cover debt under credit facility and notes.

risks.risk_name: Failure of growth strategies in new markets and products
risks.description: Strategies to expand into new geographies and product segments may fail due to delays, competition, or inability to penetrate markets.
risks.why: Growth depends on success in Brazil, India, China, and new PCC applications like papercoating pigments; delays or failures in these initiatives could hinder sales and income growth.

risks.risk_name: Risks from acquisitions including integration failures and unmet synergies
risks.description: Acquisitions may fail to deliver expected benefits due to integration challenges, cost overruns, or loss of key personnel.
risks.why: Acquisitions could incur debt, divert management attention, and face longer/more costly integration; synergies may not materialize, and potential deals may never close despite resource expenditure.

risks.risk_name: Inability to innovate or protect intellectual property
risks.description: Failure to develop new products or defend proprietary technology could erode competitive advantage and market position.
risks.why: Success depends on timely, cost-effective innovation; competitors may develop superior/cheaper alternatives, and IP theft or infringement could undermine product differentiation and revenue.

risks.risk_name: International operations exposure to political and economic instability
risks.description: Operations in countries with political or economic instability face risks including inflation, currency fluctuations, tariffs, expropriation, civil unrest, terrorism, war, and unstable legal systems.
risks.why: The company has significant production facilities outside the U.S. and operates in countries like Indonesia, Nigeria, Egypt, Turkey, Brazil, China, and South Africa, which have experienced instability; it also ceased sales to Russia after its invasion of Ukraine, with potential spillover effects on global supply chains and trade.

risks.risk_name: Foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations
risks.description: Sales, earnings, cash flows, and asset values are affected by changes in foreign currency exchange rates due to non-U.S. transactions denominated in local currencies.
risks.why: A significant portion of raw material purchases and sales outside the U.S. are denominated in foreign currencies, and non-U.S. operating expenses and income taxes are in local currencies, exposing financial results to exchange rate volatility.

risks.risk_name: Volatility in raw material costs and availability
risks.description: Critical raw materials like magnesia, lime, carbon dioxide, alumina, and petrochemicals are subject to price volatility and supply disruptions.
risks.why: The company purchases ~50% of its magnesia from China, where prices have fluctuated; petrochemical and energy price increases have already affected business, and supply may be unavailable on timely or acceptable terms.

risks.risk_name: Energy cost increases impacting production and shipping
risks.description: High energy consumption for manufacturing and shipping exposes the company to price fluctuations in electricity, diesel, natural gas, and coal.
risks.why: Production processes consume significant energy; diesel fuels mining and freight; energy costs affect raw material prices; while some PCC contracts allow cost pass-through, there is a time lag and no guarantee of recovery.

risks.risk_name: Loss of mining permits or access to ore reserves
risks.description: Mining operations depend on permits and leases that can be modified, renewed, or revoked due to regulatory or governmental actions.
risks.why: Ore reserve estimates involve subjective judgments, and permits in emerging markets like Turkey and China are subject to legal and regulatory changes that could prevent continued access to reserves.

risks.risk_name: Volatility in bulk shipping costs and container availability
risks.description: Shipping costs for bentonite and other bulk cargoes are volatile, and container availability is unreliable, impacting profitability if costs cannot be passed to customers.
risks.why: Bulk cargo shipping rates have been highly volatile; container availability has been suspect; and the company may be unable to offset increased costs through customer price increases.

risks.risk_name: Rail service interruptions and cost recovery challenges
risks.description: Rail service disruptions and inability to recover increased rail costs can hinder product shipping and hurt profitability.
risks.why: Rail service interruptions have already affected shipping, and the availability of rail service and cost recovery are beyond the company’s control.

risks.risk_name: Supply chain and logistics disruptions from government mandates
risks.description: Government mandates during public health crises or other emergencies can disrupt shipping, employee availability, and operational procedures.
risks.why: During COVID-19, government restrictions affected shipping, employee effectiveness, and facility access; similar disruptions could recur in future crises.

risks.risk_name: Compliance costs and liabilities from environmental, health, and safety regulations
risks.description: Stringent environmental, health, safety, and tax regulations expose the company to unanticipated compliance costs and legal liabilities.
risks.why: The company incurs substantial compliance costs; future regulatory changes, enforcement policies, or investigations could increase costs or restrict mining rights; and it faces ongoing litigation related to asbestos and product stewardship.

risks.risk_name: Climate-related legislation restricting greenhouse gas emissions
risks.description: Climate regulations restricting greenhouse gas emissions could increase energy costs and reduce demand for products, with limited ability to pass costs to customers.
risks.why: Manufacturing, especially PCC, uses significant energy; proposed climate laws could raise energy prices, and the company may not be able to recover these costs through pricing adjustments.

risks.risk_name: Tax liability exposure from jurisdictional earnings mix and regulatory changes
risks.description: Income tax liabilities are sensitive to the geographic distribution of earnings and changes in tax laws, treaties, or valuation of deferred tax assets.
risks.why: The company operates in multiple jurisdictions; its tax provision depends on earnings mix, and changes in tax treaties, laws, or deferred tax valuations could adversely affect liabilities.

risks.risk_name: Litigation and product liability claims, including asbestos-related cases
risks.description: Ongoing litigation, including asbestos claims tied to a subsidiary’s talc products, could result in significant settlements or judgments exceeding accrued liabilities.
risks.why: The company and subsidiaries are defendants in multiple cases seeking damages for alleged asbestos exposure from Barretts Minerals Inc. products, with potential payouts beyond current accruals.

risks.risk_name: Business disruption from the global COVID-19 pandemic
risks.description: The pandemic has caused supply chain delays, workforce disruptions, facility closures, and increased costs, with uncertain future impacts.
risks.why: COVID-19 led to travel restrictions, reduced employee availability, facility shutdowns, and logistics delays; future impacts depend on outbreak duration, variants, and containment measures, which remain unpredictable.

risks.risk_name: Production facility shutdowns due to operational hazards or government mandates
risks.description: Manufacturing facilities face hazards like explosions, fires, natural disasters, and mechanical failures, and may be closed by government mandates or safety concerns.
risks.why: Facilities are subject to chemical hazards, equipment failure, and weather events; during COVID-19, facilities were temporarily closed due to mandates or positive cases, disrupting operations.

risks.risk_name: Inadequate insurance coverage for operational hazards
risks.description: Property, business interruption, and casualty insurance may not fully cover losses from manufacturing hazards, leaving the company exposed to uninsured losses.
risks.why: Insurance policies have limitations including deductibles and coverage caps, and may not cover all risks associated with chemical handling, explosions, or environmental damage.

risks.risk_name: Seasonal demand fluctuations affecting product line revenues
risks.description: Revenues from Energy Services, Building Materials, and Processed Minerals are affected by seasonal weather patterns, reducing activity in winter months.
risks.why: Energy Services revenues are tied to Gulf of Mexico hurricane season (June–November); construction activity declines in winter, reducing demand for Building Materials and Processed Minerals.

risks.risk_name: Cybersecurity attacks disrupting operations and data integrity
risks.description: Reliance on digital systems exposes the company to cyber-attacks that can compromise data, interrupt operations, and increase mitigation costs.
risks.why: The company has previously suffered a ransomware attack; increased remote work has heightened reliance on digital systems, and insufficient protections could lead to data loss, operational disruption, or reputational harm.
